articles.title: Jayden Daniels Injury Update, Commanders QB's Target Return Date Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders reportedly hope quarterback Jayden Daniels will return for their Week 5 game against the New York Giants.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders reportedly hope quarterback Jayden Daniels will return for their Week 5 game against the New York Giants.

"The Commanders are hopeful QB Jayden Daniels—who will miss his second straight game Sunday—will return to the lineup next week against the Giants," Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported Saturday. "As expected, he's wearing a larger brace to protect his balky left elbow, and if he can get through a full week of practice without issue, expect him to play."

Daniels dislocated his left elbow in the first half of Washington's 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. It's the same elbow he dislocated last season that kept him out for seven of the final eight games.

Ahead of the Commanders' Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts, Daniels returned to practice on a limited basis. He ultimately didn't play to give his injury more time to heal, but this was an encouraging sign his absence might not last much longer.

One reason the Commanders may have felt comfortable keeping Daniels out against the Colts is how well Marcus Mariota played in Week 3. He finished with 183 passing yards and three touchdowns in a 33-31 upset win over the Seattle Seahawks.

However, Mariota suffered a knee injury against the Colts, which left Athan Kaliakmanis under center.

Given how prevalent the elbow issues have been for Daniels over the past two seasons, the Commanders want to be cautious to make sure he is at full strength before putting him back on the field.

Still, they need Daniels to reach whatever the ceiling for this team is going to be in 2026.

Daniels was 29-of-51 for 260 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions through the air in two games prior to the injury. He also ran for 100 yards on 12 carries during that period.

articles.title: NFL in London: Indianapolis Colts beat Washington Commanders 30-13 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor scores twice with Daniel Jones running in the other of the Indianapolis Colts' three scores; rookie seventh-round quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis throws his first NFL touchdown pass after Marcus Mariota leaves game injured for Washington Commanders
articles.body:
The Commanders initially had the better of things, limiting the Colts offense to 20 total yards in the first quarter as they claimed a 6-0 lead.

But an injury to QB Marcus Mariota when sacked on the play prior to Washington's second field goal proved a turning point, with third-stringer Athan Kaliakmanis - a seventh-round draft pick - unable to lead the Commanders to victory despite a couple of eye-catching plays, including a 47-yard deep-ball TD for his first in the NFL.

Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, who had two turnovers in the first half, ran in Indianapolis' third touchdown of the game early in the fourth quarter to stretch their lead to two scores - and there was to be no way back for Washington.

The NFL returns to Tottenham next Sunday for a clash between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars, who are back in action facing the Houston Texans at Wembley a week later, on Sunday October 18.

Passing: Daniel Jones, 19/34, 143 yards, 1 rushing TD, 1 INT

Rushing: Jonathan Taylor, 20 carries, 95 yards, 2 TDs

Receiving: Laquon Treadwell, 9 catches, 42 yards

Passing: Athan Kaliakmanis, 15/33, 186 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Rushing: Marcus Mariota, 1 carry, 35 yards

Receiving: Dyami Brown, 3 catches, 65 yards

The Colts fell behind early when Jones lost the football after he was accidentally tripped by his own team-mate, with the Commanders scoring a field goal after Odafe Oweh recovered the ball at the 20-yard line.

Mariota, filling in for injured starting QB Jayden Daniels, left the game with a knee injury when sacked on the play prior to Washington's second field goal.

Kaliakmanis came in, the 223rd overall pick from the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and though he found the going tough early on his NFL debut, Colts veteran Jones was similarly struggling and was picked off by Rasul Douglas.

But the Colts soon took over again on downs after the Commanders' call to go for it on fourth down from their own 46-yard line. It would prove a poor decision, helping set up Taylor's opening TD for Indianapolis to see them into a lead that they stretched to four by the half with the first of Spencer Shrader's three field goals. Taylor celebrated his score by pantomiming drinking tea in the end zone.

Kaliakmanis threw a costly interception early in the third quarter, with Taylor's second five-yard scoring run of the game then making it 17-6.

Kaliakmanis bounced back on the next drive, though, hitting Treylon Burks on a stunning, 47-yard touchdown pass deep down the left sideline that closed the gap as Burks got past star cornerback Sauce Gardner.

But the Colts (2-2) answered back with further Shrader field goals either side of Jones' touchdown run from four yards out early in the fourth quarter.

articles.title: “It’s a full commitment from the full family”: How Patrick Mahomes’ ACL rehab tested Brittany Mahomes strength at home with their 3 kids
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes spent much of his 2026 offseason working through a serious knee injury.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes spent much of his 2026 offseason working through a serious knee injury. While the Chiefs quarterback focused on his recovery, Brittany Mahomes took on more at home with their three children. Mahomes recently opened up about that side of his comeback, giving Brittany credit for keeping their family routine going while he spent long hours at the rehab facility.The comment came as Mahomes prepared for Kansas City’s Week 4 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. Speaking with Mitch Holthus on “The Chiefs Kingdom Show” at Arrowhead Stadium earlier this week, Mahomes explained that his recovery affected the whole family. He also revealed why getting back to his children became one of his biggest personal goals. How Brittany Mahomes took over more at home while Patrick Mahomes focused on his recoveryMahomes did not go through his rehab alone, but his wife carried a different part of the load.In a recent interview, Mahomes explained that Brittany had to take on more responsibility because he spent much of the offseason away from home. The quarterback said he spent about seven hours a day at the rehab facility when the family would normally spend that time together on vacation or back in Texas.“She had to kind of take on that role on even more because I wasn’t at the house,” Mahomes said during “The Chiefs Kingdom Show.”That meant Brittany handled more of the daily routine with their three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden. Sterling is 5, Bronze is 3, and Golden is 20 months old, according to the Heavy report.Mahomes then gave his wife direct credit for keeping the household together.“It’s a full commitment from the full family,” he said during the same Arrowhead interview. He added that Brittany did “a great job” leading the household while he worked at the rehab facility.Brittany later shared a clip of Mahomes’ comments on her Instagram Stories and responded, “Would do anything for my babies and my husband.”That response added another layer to Mahomes’ comments. His return to football required daily work from him, but family life still needed attention while he spent those hours rehabbing. Why getting back to his kids became a major part of Patrick Mahomes’ comebackThe family angle goes beyond Brittany handling more at home. Mahomes has also explained how his injury changed his role as a father.During Chiefs training camp on July 24, 2026, Steve Walls asked Mahomes about the toughest mental hurdle during his rehab. Mahomes did not point to missing football. Instead, he talked about his children.“Honestly, the toughest part was at the beginning, not being able to get up and chase my kids around,” Mahomes said at training camp.He explained that being active with his children has always been important to him. Once his recovery allowed him to move around with them again, that progress gave him another reason to keep pushing.Mahomes specifically mentioned Bronze’s T-ball games and Sterling’s soccer activities. Being able to attend those moments gave him a clear sign that his recovery was moving forward.Mahomes suffered the knee injury during Kansas City’s Week 15 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers in December 2025. He later spent roughly nine months working toward his return, with his children becoming part of the motivation behind that process.Now, as the Chiefs move through the 2026 season, Mahomes’ comeback carries a personal story beyond the football field. His rehab demanded long hours from him, while Brittany helped keep their family life moving. articles.title: NFL Week 4 Live Fantasy Football Start 'Em Sit 'Em Lineup Advice and Latest Injury Updates
articles.summary: The calendar has turned to October, and for different fantasy football managers that means different things.
articles.body:
The calendar has turned to October, and for different fantasy football managers that means different things.

For some, the first month of the season has been a breeze. They have rostered players like Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs or Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. As those stars have piled up stats, they have piled up points—and victories.

For others, however, things haven't gone as smoothly. The only things that have piled up are injuries—injuries that have blasted holes in starting lineups. Highly-drafted players have disappointed. Losses are mounting. The season is in danger of coming off the rails.

Whether you are rolling or reeling, Bleacher Report is here to help you start Week 4 with a bang—with the injury news, lineup advice and fantasy tips that will either keep the good times rolling or end that depressing early-season skid.

WR Terry McLaurin, Washington Commanders (Hamstring)

RB Jadarian Price, Seattle Seahawks (Chest -- IR)

WR DeVonta Smith, Philadelphia Eagles (Hamstring)

WR Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (Groin)

It appears that Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers will stay play against the Chiefs in Week 4, but being added to the injury report on gameday with an illness does not inspire the warm and fuzzies--especially with a 4:25 PM kick.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was already coming off his worst fantasy effort of the season in last week's loss to the Chicago Bears.

Now he draws a poor fantasy matchup for his position short his top wideout and starting tight end.

Hurts is a low-end QB1 in Week 4--at best.

The New Orleans Saints have also surrendered the fourth-most PPR points to tight ends this season.

But starting Atlanta's Kyle Pitts in fantasy feels a lot like Charlie Brown barreling toward a football--he knows what's going to happen, but he can't help himself.

Last week, Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love had the best game of his young career--26 touches, 109 yards and a score.

The third pick in the 2026 NFL Draft should keep the positive momentum going this week against the Giants--New York has been kind to opposing running backs this season, allowing the likes of Javonte Williams of the Cowboys and Kyren Williams of the Rams to post fat stat lines.

Given all the injuries at running back, some fantasy managers have little recourse in Week 4 but to roll out New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara on Monday night and hope for the best.

"The best" probably won't be much. The opponents they have faced have played a part, but the Atlanta Falcons have allowed just 47.7 yards per game on the ground this year--fewest in the NFL.

As expected, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is active against the Eagles after missing the last two games with a groin injury.

And there was much rejoicing--except from Davante Adams managers.

Fantasy managers with shares of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley are starting him in Week 4. That goes without saying.

But Barkley already had a tough matchup with a Rams defense allowing just 101.3 yards per game on the ground, and now the Eagles will be short right tackle Lane Johnson, who was a late scratch for personal reasons.

No surprises here, which is a good thing.

Of course, that may only be because we already knew that 47 fantasy-relevant players were out this week.

London games are the bane of fantasy managers.

Brycen Tremaine isn't a fantasy play for the faint of heart--prior to last week he didn't have a target, much less a catch.

But Tremaine caught four passes for 83 yards against the Browns in week 3, the Panthers WR corps has been hit hard by injuries and the Detroit defense couldn't cover a wall with paint.

He's literally the only fantasy asset playing in the London game who has done anything.

It has been a slow start to the 2026 season for Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud--he enters Week 4 barely inside the top-20 in fantasy points among signal-callers.

But Stroud will have No. 1 receiver Nico Collins back Sunday against Dallas, and the Cowboys have allowed the third-most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season.

If Stroud can't make some hay in this matchup, it's hard to justify rostering him--let alone starting him.

OK, so calling Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson a "sleeper" may be pushing it--with Jadarian Price headed to injured reserve, Wilson was one of the most added players in fantasy this week.

But per Jamey Eisenberg of CBS Sports , Wilson has nine games in his career with double digits in carries. He has scored at least 11.7 PPR points in six of those outings.

It wouldn't surprise this writer if Mike Evans is active in Week 4--the veteran wideout has a history of playing through injuries.

But it also wouldn't be a surprise if he sits, and with the San Francisco 49ers taking on the Denver Broncos in the late window fantasy managers need to have a Plan B at the ready.

Can I interest you in a gently-used Cooper Kupp?

Three weeks into the 2026 season, no team has allowed more fantasy points to quarterbacks than the Detroit Lions.

All three quarterbacks who have faced the Lions this year have thrown at least three touchdown passes.

Young entered Week 4 fourth among quarterbacks in points, and a top-five outing is a real possibility Sunday night.

Sunday morning's London game between the Commanders and Colts may cause an international incident between the United States and the UK.

But at least Jonathan Taylor managers got a score out of it.

Ollie Gordon was one of this week's hot waiver wire pickups this week after De'Von Achane tore his ACL.

but in their zeal to grab any running back with a pulse, fantasy managers overlooked a couple of things.

The first is that Gordon was a full-time back last week only because Jaylen Wright was inactive. Wright is expected to play Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings, and he's listed as the starting running back on Miami's depth chart.

The second is that the Dolphins are terrible, so it may not matter who the lead back is. Wright and Gordon will likely split a workload that wasn't doing anything for Achane.

Neither Miami back is more than a desperation flex.

The Colts offense is unwatchable right now.

Daniel Jones has completed six of 14 attempts for 22 yards with a lost fumble and a pick.

Colts tight end Tyler Warren has as many targets as I do.

What? I'm on a tight ends kick, apparently.

Given the rip that Travis Kelce has been on to start the 2026 season, you don't need me to tell you to start him--Kelce entered Week 4 second at the position in PPR points.

But the old man's a safe bet to hit double-digit PPR points for the fourth time in as many weeks--only two teams have allowed more points to the position this season.

Last week against the Cleveland Browns, Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller saw eight targets, catching five passes for 51 yards.

With Jalen Coker (quad) likely out Sunday night, Waller should see a similar target share against a Detroit Lions defense that couldn't cover a bed with a sheet.

Fantasy managers with shares of Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III are likely not especially happy with the news that Tyson Bagent will draw the start for the Chicago Bears at quarterback in Week 4 and not Case Keenum. But it offers a glimmer of hope that maybe a switch under center will get tight end Colston Loveland going after a dreadful start to the season.

But Sunday's matchup with the Jets isn't a good one--Gang Green has allowed the third-fewest PPR points to tight ends so far this season.

Fantasy managers hoping for a big game from Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs Sunday morning with Terry McLaurin out may have wished they had slept in.

I'm not sure Athan Kaliakmanis is a real person.

Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers racked up six catches for 84 yards in Brazil last week--an impressive stat line given that he played just 21 snaps.

Flowers' fantasy managers will be glad to hear that Sunday against the Titans he should be on the field a lot more--he's expected to play without limitations in Week 4.

Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker got off to a torrid start over the first two weeks of the 2026 season.

But Coker left last week's loss to the Cleveland Browns with a quad injury, and that injury is expected to sideline him Sunday night against the Lions.

Don't wait to replace him in fantasy lineups--there isn't much in the way of backup plans playing in that contest.

For fantasy managers who spent their first-round pick on Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, hearing that the fourth-year pro would return Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles is good news.

Hearing that he won't be limited is even better.

Of course, for Davante Adams managers the news is a little less welcome--but them's the breaks.

Given the sorry state of the Tennessee offense, starting any Titans player in fantasy doesn't inspire a lot of confidence.

But many fantasy managers are fresh out of options in the backfield, and Tyjae Spears is expected to play Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens despite an ankle injury.

Chargers WR Ladd McConkey Expected to Play

The good news is that Los Angeles wide receiver Ladd McConkey is expected to play through his foot injury Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks.

The bad news is that he'll be playing for the floundering Chargers.

With wide receiver DeVonta Smith expected to miss multiple games with a hamstring injury, it will fall to Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon to serve as the Eagles' top two wide receivers Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams.

However, the Rams are a below-average fantasy matchup for both wide receivers and quarterbacks, so whether it's those young pass-catchers or Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, Week 4 could be a tricky one.

This isn't to say you should sit Hurts. But if you have a Plan B with a solid matchup it's not the worst idea ever.

Emmanuel Wilson was already a hot name on waiver wires after Seattle running back Jadarian Price was ruled out for Week 4 with a chest injury. Now that Price is on injured reserve though, the Seattle backfield is looking--less than ideal.

Zach Charbonnet has been designated for return, although whether that's Week 5 or Week 6 remains to be seen. Until then, it will fall to Wilson and George Holani to hold down the fort in the Seahawks backfield.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba should see approximately all the targets ever Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers

Nothing like having a star player inactive in a 9:30 AM start in London to start the week off right.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. expected to play for Cowboys in Week 4 after missing start of season with back injury
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr. is feeling better after a mid-week trade to the Cowboys.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is healed. After missing the start of the season due to a back injury, Porter is expected to play in Week 4 after being traded to the Cowboys, according to ESPN.

Porter, however, is expected to have his snaps limited during the contest.

It will mark the first game all season in which Porter has played. The 26-year-old missed the first three weeks of the regular season due to both back and conditioning issues. Despite being able to put in work during practices, Porter was constantly ruled out on game days by the Pittsburgh Steelers after missing time in the offseason due to a contract dispute.

That dispute ultimately resulted in the Steelers trading Porter to the Cowboys on Wednesday. The Cowboys sent a sixth-round pick and a second-round pick to the Steelers as part of the deal.

Following the trade, Porter was not listed among the Cowboys' injuries and received no injury designation on the team's final report, suggesting he would suit up in Week 4 against the Houston Texans.

While there's an uncharitable read on the situation that suggests Porter was never truly hurt and was sitting out over his contract situation in Pittsburgh, the limited snap count for Porter in Week 4 does suggest there are legitimate concerns about immediately throwing him into a game.

Porter, who is in the final year of his rookie contract, was at odds with the Steelers all offseason over a contract extension. There was a hard deadline on a deal getting done, as the Steelers — generally — do not negotiate contracts during the season. That deadline passed without a deal, putting Porter and the team at an impasse.

That impasse was solved with Wednesday's trade. Though he still doesn't have a contract extension, Porter will reportedly take the field for the Cowboys in Week 4. If he can go out and turn in a strong season, Porter should eventually get the mega-contract he's seeking, whether from the Cowboys or from another franchise once he hits the free-agent market.

articles.title: Tony Pollard among NFL trade deadline targets to watch, per report
articles.summary: ESPN reported that Titans running back Tony Pollard is a player to watch in the weeks leading into the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline is still more than a month away, but chatter is already starting after a couple trades this week.

ESPN's Adam Schefter, reporting on the network's "Sunday NFL Countdown" pregame show on Oct. 4, mentioned Titans running back Tony Pollard as a player to watch among NFL trade targets before the Nov. 10 deadline.

Pollard, 29, has rushed for at least 1,000 yards in each of the last four seasons, including the last two with Tennessee.

The Memphis alum "fits the profile" as a trade target, Schefter reported, given the Titans' slow start and his contract.

Pollard is in the final year of a three-year deal signed in 2024 as the Titans aimed to replace Derrick Henry. He has a base salary of $6.74 million this year with $510,000 in roster bonuses spread across the season, per Spotrac.

The veteran back has been the Titans' clear No. 1 back through three weeks in terms of touches and production despite Tyjae Spears playing 44% of offensive snaps.

Tennessee also has rookie running back Nicholas Singleton and veterans Julius Chestnut and Michael Carter on the roster.

articles.title: Marcus Mariota ruled out in Week 4 with right knee injury, Commanders already down Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: The Commanders are already without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels in Week 4.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders came into Week 4 dealing with multiple significant injuries on offense. Early in the contest, they were dealt another one, as quarterback Marcus Mariota was forced to leave the game after a first-quarter sack.

The play occurred on Washington's second drive of the game. With the team deep in Indianapolis Colts' territory, Mariota was sacked on a third-and-goal. The Commanders were forced to kick a field goal at the end of the drive, taking a 6-0 lead.

Mariota headed to the blue tent on the sideline before being taken back to the locker room. The Commanders eventually announced a right knee injury for Mariota. He was initially deemed questionable to return before being ruled out before the start of the third quarter.

On the team's next drive, Athan Kaliakmanis entered the game as the team's starting quarterback. The drive marked Kaliakmanis' NFL debut. The team selected him out of Rutgers in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft.

Mariota's injury comes at an awful time for the Commanders. The team came into Sunday's contest without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, backup running back Rashaad White and No. 1 receiver Terry McLaurin.

While the Commanders' offense stalled twice with Mariota under center — settling for field goals — the veteran had shown some big-play potential before going down. Prior to leaving the game, Mariota had a 35-yard rush and found running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on a short gain that wound up going for 35 yards.

Kaliakmanis could not get anything going offensively for the Commanders, leading to the team falling behind 10-6 at halftime.

articles.title: Andy Dalton Demoted to Eagles QB3 in Latest Rumors After Costly INT vs. Bears
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles veteran quarterback Andy Dalton is facing consequences for his mistake in last week's loss to the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles veteran quarterback Andy Dalton is facing consequences for his mistake in last week's loss to the Chicago Bears.

After his lone throw of the game resulted in an interception at the goal line, Dalton was demoted to Philadelphia's QB3 behind Jalen Hurts and Tanner McKee for Sunday's matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Hurts had driven Philadelphia deep into Chicago territory midway through the second quarter before being pulled from the field to be checked for a concussion following a late hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson. After Dalton took over, the Eagles got down to Chicago's 2-yard line, but he fired a pass to the back of the end zone on third-and-goal that was picked off by Bears rookie safety Dillon Thieneman.

Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion took the blame for Dalton's interception, telling reporters on Thursday, "Obviously, with the outcome, it's one certainly I wish I could have back if I could do it over again. It was a call that we felt confident in throughout the week. We had a good week's worth of practice. It's something Andy has banked reps on, so I felt like it was something he could execute."

A 16-year veteran, Dalton was traded to the Eagles from the Carolina Panthers this past offseason. He competed with McKee for the backup role behind Hurts throughout training camp, and he surprisingly beat out the 26-year-old for the job.

After losing his position to McKee entering Week 4, Dalton will continue to provide veteran guidance as the Eagles try to return to title contention this season.

articles.title: Colts Beat Commanders, Box Score Stats, Highlights for JT, Daniel Jones, Kaliakmanis, Top Players
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have seemingly put their 0-2 start in the rearview mirror.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have seemingly put their 0-2 start in the rearview mirror.

Indianapolis defeated the Washington Commanders 30-13 on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. It improved to 2-2 with a second straight win, while the Commanders fell to 1-3 after they were forced to turn to seventh-round draft pick Athan Kaliakmanis under center following Marcus Mariota's knee injury.

Jayden Daniels was already out, and the third-stringer was unable to counter multiple touchdowns from star Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, who made NFL history by accumulating the most rushing yards and touchdowns in international games.

The Commanders were already facing an uphill battle coming into the game with Daniels (elbow) and Terry McLaurin (hamstring) sidelined by injuries. Things went from bad to worse in the first quarter when Mariota suffered the injury on a sack.

Enter the rookie from Rutgers in Kaliakmanis, who struggled handling some of the initial pressure from the Indianapolis defense. The last thing Washington could afford with a third-string quarterback in the game was self-inflicted mistakes, but that was a key theme of the first half.

It turned the ball over on downs inside its own territory while holding a 6-0 lead and then committed an unnecessary roughness penalty on a failed Colts' third-down attempt on the ensuing possession. That kept things alive for Indianapolis, and it took full advantage of the mistake when Taylor scored the game's first touchdown.

Daniel Jones also settled in some on the drive after a horrible start that saw him lose a fumble on the game's first possession and throw an ugly interception to Rasul Douglas.

But the Jones roller coaster was nothing compared to the Kaliakmanis one in the second half.

It seemed like the game was slipping away from the third-stringer when he started the second half by throwing an interception to Jaylon Carlies that the Colts turned into another Taylor touchdown.

However, he responded with a stunning 47-yard touchdown pass to Treylon Burks before another deep ball to Dyami Brown on the next possession. He wasn't hesitant to unleash deep balls and was getting more comfortable, but a big sack ended the scoring threat after the Brown completion.

Kaliakmanis also connected with Antonio Williams for an 87-yard touchdown where the wide receiver did most of the work, but it was nullified by penalty.

The overturned touchdown ended up being Washington's final realistic chance of keeping pace, as the Colts marched 52 yards on nine plays for a touchdown on the ensuing possession to open a two-score lead. This time it was Jones who ran it in, and he also directed a field-goal drive in the fourth quarter after Kaliakmanis turned it over on downs.

It was a valiant effort at times for Kaliakmanis, but it wasn't enough to leave London with the win ahead of the upcoming showdown with the rival New York Giants.

As for the Colts, they return home and host the Pittsburgh Steelers as they look to sustain their momentum.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Teases Changes to NFL Schedule for Rivalry Games
articles.summary: Ahead of a rare meeting between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones recently suggested that in-state rivalry games could become more of a norm soon.
articles.body:
Ahead of a rare meeting between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones recently suggested that in-state rivalry games could become more of a norm soon.

Sunday's matchup between the two Texas teams will be just the eighth showdown between the Cowboys and Texans since Houston joined the NFL in 2002. During Friday's radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, Jones indicated that the league is considering scheduling more geographic rivalry games between teams from opposing conferences.

"You can add that in the mix, and I'm not saying it's not in the mix," Jones said (h/t Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk. "It's just that other things come up and you have a different reason for the scheduling. We obviously have a rotation involved that is the best as far as fair, complete competition year-in, year-out, around the entire league. But it's certainly something that I would look at.

"And I wouldn't just narrow it down to Dallas and Houston," he continued. "I'd look at the entire league, you saw a game on TV [Thursday] night between Cleveland and Pittsburgh. They're in the same division, but those kinds of proximities, those kinds of 'my town against your town, and who's the best town?' Which I think is a fundamental of our game of football. 'My town against your town. My school against your school.' That's a big part of it. It's hard to emulate any place but in the United States to get that rolling."

Other options for such rivalry games include the New York Jets and New York Giants, the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers, the Baltimore Ravens and Washington Commanders, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Philadelphia Eagles, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Jacksonville Jaguars, and more.

If Jones gets his wish, it will be interesting to see if the NFL tries to implement these rivalry games as part of the current 17-game schedule, or as a way to increase the regular season to 18 games.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Calls Out Giants After Surprise Release, Explains What 'Broke Me TF Down'
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. says the New York Giants "gave me the run along" with their decision to release him Tuesday after he made the initial roster.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. says the New York Giants "gave me the run along" with their decision to release him Tuesday after he made the initial roster.

The veteran wide receiver provided his perspective through Instagram comments and explained it "broke me tf down" when his son was talking about how happy he was before knowing Beckham was no longer on the team.

He also said, "idk why they even gave me the run along, I coulda really been playing this year somewhere and making a impact."

Notably, Beckham's comments come after NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Giants and Beckham came to a "mutual" decision to part ways.

"This gives him an opportunity to catch on with a team in a better situation, where his talents can be better utilized," Schultz added.

Beckham's latest comments didn't make it seem like a mutual decision, and they also come after head coach John Harbaugh was matter-of-fact about the situation.

"We just weren't getting enough. It just wasn't working for us," Harbaugh told reporters Wednesday. "I wanted to be able to give more; I wanted him to be able to do more. I wanted to get him on the field more.

"I'm not hiding anything. It's not Watergate. We're trying to be the best team we can be this week."

Beckham's return to the Giants seemed like a full-circle moment for his career, as he starred for the franchise during his first five seasons. He was a three-time Pro Bowler and the Offensive Rookie of the Year during that span and also surpassed 1,300 receiving yards in each of his first three seasons.

Yet the version of Beckham who started the 2026 campaign was not the same as the one who was so unstoppable early in his career.

He failed to record a catch and had just one target in New York's first three games.

Instead, wide receivers Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields and Darnell Mooney, along with tight end Isaiah Likely, have been far more involved in the aerial attack. And now Beckham is left looking for his next stop after his reunion didn't work in New York.

articles.title: Joe Mixon Reportedly Visiting Seahawks After Posting Cryptic Video amid Injury Rehab
articles.summary: After missing the entire 2025 season while recovering from a leg injury, veteran running back Joe Mixon appears to be eyeing an NFL comeback.
articles.body:
After missing the entire 2025 season while recovering from a leg injury, veteran running back Joe Mixon appears to be eyeing an NFL comeback.

Jay Glazer (h/t Underdog NFL ) reported on this week's episode of Fox NFL Sunday that Mixon is visiting with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Mixon recently posted a video for his company, OneSock, and said at the end, "I'm back, baby!"

Mixon last played for the Houston Texans in 2024, appearing in 14 games and running for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns on 245 carries to earn his second career Pro Bowl selection. He spent the first seven years of his career with the Cincinnati Bengals, surpassing the 1,000-yard mark four times.

The Seahawks have an opening in their backfield after placing starting running back Jadarian Price on injured reserve on Saturday due to a chest injury. The rookie ball-carrier had started all three of Seattle's games, recording 119 rushing yards on 28 carries. He hadn't scored a touchdown, and he lost two fumbles.

"By no means is this JD's fault or anything like that," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Friday, per ESPN's Brady Henderson . "This is just what happens in football. Unfortunately, injuries happen. He can't control these things. He's done everything we've asked him to do since he got here. He's had a great attitude. He's been a great teammate. He has a great future. He's going to play great football for us when he comes back, whenever that is … It's just unfortunate."

Price will miss at least the next four games, leaving Emanuel Wilson and George Holani as Seattle's top available running backs. Fourth-year pro Zack Charbonnet is still working his way back from a torn ACL suffered during last season's playoffs.

The Seahawks are taking on the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, so they will likely wait a few days before making a decision on adding Mixon to the roster.

articles.title: Jason Kelce calls the Commanders the 'Redskins' during game, immediately apologizes so as to not get canceled
articles.summary: Jason Kelce accidentally called the Commanders the Redskins during an NFL Network broadcast, prompting Dave Pasch to quickly correct him on air.
articles.body: Jason Kelce acted as if he committed an unpardonable broadcasting sin Sunday afternoon while serving as a booth analyst for NFL Network during the Washington Commanders game against the Indianapolis Colts. Kelce's sin? He called the team in burgundy and gold the Washington Redskins. Gasp! CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL BATTLES NEWSOM'S STATE LAW ORDERING IT TO CHANGE 'INDIANS' MASCOT This is actually nothing if you're a normal person who is aware the Commanders were the Redskins for decades until that name got canceled by an outcry to mostly liberal voices claiming "Redskins" is a racist insult. (Native Americans have both agreed and vehemently disagreed the term is racist – it mostly depends on what group with an agenda one asks). Anyway, back to Kelce. Look, he's still trying to settle into his broadcasting role three years after retiring from the Philadelphia Eagles. He was a 13-year NFL center of the highest caliber, so he's outstanding at explaining offensive line play. This booth analyst gig is mostly new for Kelce and he got all fired up explaining the Commanders' play in the secondary. "Washington's secondary has been great on third down," Kelce said under replays of plays by the unit. "...When you're in man to man coverage, it just takes one missed tackle, and that can turn into a huge play. "The Redskins right now are doing a great job of not only staying tight, but making the play when the ball is in the receiver's hand and keeping it short of the sticks." Play-by-play announcer Dave Pasch immediately chimed in, "Commanders. You did it." Oh noes, Kelce is in trouble. Or at least he acted like it. "What'd I do?" Kelce asked. "You said Redskins," Pasch said, repeating that nickname that is both beloved and blackballed. "Oh, my gosh!" Kelce exclaimed. "I almost made it out." The three men in the booth that included Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner as another analyst, apparently talked about the possibility of inadvertently using the Redskins name on air before the game. "Yeah, the three of us had a little gentleman's bet who would be first," Pasch said. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! And all this shows the utter stupidity of the whole name change thing. If one were to take a poll of whether the Redskins should continue to be called the Redskins, as they were in Washington since 1937 to 2020, it is likely a large portion of respondents would definitely want the traditional nickname to return. And, yes, there are people who would still want the old nickname banished to the memory of what they believe was a racist time. Washington owner Josh Harris is apparently in this group, and he gets the final call. But one simply cannot erase history – although some people try. The Redskins were beloved in Washington. Kelce played against them during nine of his 13 seasons with that team. TAYLOR HEINICKE RETIRES FROM THE NFL WITH A FAREWELL SALUTE TO THE WASHINGTON REDSKINS Many players who wore the Indian head helmet logo inspired by Blackfeet Chief John Two Guns White Calf and heard the, "Hail to the Redskins," fight song echo in their ears during home games, continue to hold allegiance to the Redskins nickname. The NFL Network booth, led by Pasch's lighthearted approach to this flub, struck the right tone. Kelce's apology? Relax, bro. Liberals may not like it. But Diron Talbert, Dave Butz, Darryl Grant and Jonathan Allen aren't coming after you. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Hot mic catches Jalen Hurts candidly calling teammate off wrong position before censors pick it up: 'Get off the f***ing ball'
articles.summary: The Fox network censor button wasn't quick enough on this one.
articles.body:
The Fox network censor button wasn't quick enough on this one.

Early during Sunday's game between the Los Angles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles, Eagles wide receiver Elijah Moore was on the line of scrimmage, covering up tight end E.J. Jenkins. This isn't where he was supposed to be.

Thankfully for the Eagles, quarterback Jalen Hurts picked up on it before it became a problem.

On second-and-7 during Philadelphia's first possession, Hurts looked to his left pre-snap and saw Moore out of position.

"Get off the f***ing ball," Hurts said as an on-field Fox mic caught the instruction loud and clear.

Moore then went into motion, and the Eagles got off the snap with no issue. Unfortunately for the Eagles, the play picked up just one yard, and they ended up punting two snaps later.

Fox play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt heard it along with everybody else and acknowledged it on the broadcast.

"Uh-oh," Burkhardt said. "That didn't sound good."

This isn't the first broadcast featuring Burkhardt and color commentator Tom Brady this season that involved some not-safe-for network-TV language. Last time, though, it came from Brady instead of a player on the field.

articles.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick picks off Bears for Jets' first interception since 2024 season
articles.summary: The Jets last intercepted a pass in the 2024 season.
articles.body:
The New York Jets finally ended their streak of games without an interception in Week 4, as All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent in the second quarter.

Bagent was targeting second-year tight end Colston Loveland, but Fitzpatrick jumped the route and returned the interception for 27 yards to set the Jets up at the Bears' 34-yard line. They were unable to capitalize with a touchdown but did get points on the board off the interception, as kicker Jason Sanders drilled a 36-yard field goal.

It was the team's first interception in 636 pass attempts faced — the longest streak without an interception in NFL history. They didn't log a single interception in the entire 2025 season, meaning this is the team's first pick under head coach Aaron Glenn.

Safety Ashtyn Davis, now with the San Francisco 49ers, was the last Jets player to intercept a ball, nabbing two picks against Tyler Huntley in the team's 2024 regular-season finale against the Miami Dolphins. That was Jan. 5, 2025 — 637 days ago.

Fitzpatrick is in his ninth NFL season and first with the New York Jets. He missed Weeks 2 and 3 after suffering a groin injury early in the season opener, wasting no time getting back in the mix before coming down with that pick — his 22nd career interception.

articles.title: Eagles WR Darius Cooper turns would-be interception into TD with wild catch vs. Rams
articles.summary: This was an Eagles touchdown instead of a Rams interception.
articles.body:
Eagles wide receiver Darius Cooper broke wide open in the end zone Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams.

He ended up securing the score in spectacular and harder-than-expected fashion.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts was under pressure on the pass play while rolling to his right. He saw Cooper, but wasn't able to get off an on-target pass. Instead, he floated a ball short while passing off his back foot that gave Rams safety Quentin Lake a shot at the ball.

Lake jumped at the goal line and got his hands on the ball. But it was just out of his reach to pull it down, and it bounced off his fingertips into the hands of Cooper, who'd leapt behind him in an effort to grab the ball.

Cooper bobbled the ball in traffic as he landed back toward the turf. But he never let the ball hit the ground. When he landed in the end zone, Cooper had gained control of the ball for an unlikely touchdown and one of the wildest catches of the NFL season.

Here's another look showing Cooper fighting to gain control of the ball as he fell to the turf.

The score was the second of the season and the second of his career for Cooper. It was certainly one to remember. And it gave the Eagles a 13-3 first-half lead in a critical game against the fellow NFC hopeful Rams. Cooper later caught a less-spectacular TD seconds before halftime to put Philadelphia up 20-10.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase Injured, Latest on Bengals WR's Status and Timeline to Return from Concussion

The Cincinnati Bengals will be without one of their top playmakers for the second half of Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Chase later took to social media to express support for his team:

Chase was off to a solid start with three catches for 27 yards on three targets prior to the setback.

He is one of the best players in the entire league, so even a talented offense with other playmakers like Cincinnati's will struggle to replicate his production. The LSU product led the NFL in catches (127), receiving yards (1,708) and touchdown catches (17) during the 2024 campaign.

It was more of the same last season as an All-Pro First-Team selection with 125 catches for 1,412 yards and eight touchdowns.

Fortunately for the Bengals, they have another star receiver in Tee Higgins who can be Joe Burrow's go-to option while Chase is sidelined. Dohnte Meyers also figures to see more targets, while tight end Mike Gesicki is a reliable option.

In fact, Gesicki scored a touchdown in the third quarter of Sunday's contest when Chase was not on the field.

While those playmakers can help keep the offense afloat with Burrow running the show, the Bengals still need Chase back and healthy if they are going to reach their full potential and compete for a deep playoff run in the AFC.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson leaves Ravens-Titans game with ankle injury, replaced by Tyler Huntley in second half
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game with an ankle injury and was replaced at the start of the second half by backup Tyler Huntley.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game with an ankle injury and was replaced at the start of the second half by backup Tyler Huntley.

Jackson appeared to sustain the injury on a sack late in the first half against the Tennessee Titans, and Huntley took the field to lead Baltimore's offense to start the second. The Ravens officially ruled Jackson as questionable to return with an ankle injury.

Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson chased Jackson down from behind for a sack on the final offensive play of the first half. Jackson was able to stand up from the tackle and walk off the field. It wasn't apparent in the moment that he'd sustained an injury.

But slow-motion replay showed that Jackson's left ankle got caught up and twisted under Johnson's body as Johnson sacked him from behind. And Jackson wasn't able to return to the field to start the third quarter.

The severity and precise nature of Jackson's injury weren't initially clear. Baltimore led 24-7 when Huntley took over at quarterback, reducing pressure on Baltimore's offense with its two-time MVP quarterback on the sideline.

Jackson off to another MVP-like start to the season

Baltimore entered Sunday with a chance to join the Cleveland Browns at 3-1 atop the AFC North. Jackson, of course, is a significant piece of Baltimore's hopes in the division and beyond. He was off to another strong start to his season prior to Sunday's injury.

Jackson entered Sunday's game having completed 69.7% of his passes for 248.3 yards per game with 4 touchdowns and 1 interception. He led the NFL in both yards per attempt (9.8) and yards per completion (14.1). He'd added 124 yards (7.3 ypa) and 1 touchdown on the ground.

Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns in the first half against the Titans.

The Ravens are certainly hoping that Jackson's injury won't linger. Baltimore has upcoming games against the Falcons, Browns, Bengals, Bills and Jaguars.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr laments his short-lived return to the New York Giants: 'I should have known better'
articles.summary: Odell Beckham accused the New York Giants of giving him "the run along" after his release, claiming the team used him for money on a vet minimum deal.
articles.body: It was nice while it lasted for Odell Beckham's fateful return to the New York Giants. When the club released him last week, his silence suggested he was appreciative of the opportunity and the time that the reunion lasted. Then Beckham took to a fan's Instagram account on Saturday and the narrative changed completely. EX-NFL STAR BELIEVES ODELL BECKHAM JR 'STILL BETTER THAN MOST OF THE RECEIVERS' IN NFL AS HE RETURNS TO GIANTS Yes, welcome to 2026 when fans can post their complaints about an NFL franchise's coach, general manager and business decisions, and a disgruntled former player can join the conversation and agree. Beckham is apparently agreeing with the premise that the Giants used him, and paid minimally for it in return. That was surprising. "I'm super smart!!!! But I didn't see this one, my brotha," Beckham complained in his reply to the post. "They got me!!!" "They won on top of the money u talkin [about], I made them. I came in HUMBLY took vet min then EARNED my spot [and] didn’t say nothing bout no $$$ which I [know] make for everybody "Ima tell u this ima grown man and this [sh-t] didn’t hurt me but it did when they cut me like that cause part of me is like I shoulda known better." GIANTS WORKING OUT MULTIPLE RECEIVERS INCLUDING ODELL BECKHAM JR, WHILE EAGLES LOOK TO TRADE AJ BROWN Beckham signed a one-year veterans salary benefit deal with the Giants. That meant the team didn't have to pay him the veteran minimum and there was no guaranteed money. The deal was worth $1.3 million. And it was a fun story for a minute. Beckham originally played for the Giants from 2014-18 and was something of a prince in the city for a time. His return was seen as a warm homecoming, with Beckham saying he never wanted to leave and was happy to be back. He didn't even demand his own number back. But the return was more interesting in the press than on the field because Beckham, 33, was active for three games but caught zero passes after being targeted just once. Beckham was released on Sept. 29. And then the sting of the release hit days later. "Now let me [tell] u the [real] deal truth [that] hurt my heart to the core is [coming] home and seeing my son and how happy he was with no idea of what happened and talkin' [about] my job [and] jersey number 13 broke me [the f–k] down," Beckham wrote. Beckham is accusing the Giants of giving him "the run along," and is upset by that because it meant he couldn't pursue opportunities on other teams through training camp, the preseason, and most of September. "[I don't know] why they even gave me the run along. I [could have] really been playing this year somewhere and making [an] impact and I mean that from a person whose humbled by God and life." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! One supposes Beckham feels better unburdening himself by making public all that's on his mind. But this might not be the wise move. That's because releasing a player is as temporary as signing him. The Giants could easily consider a Beckham return if circumstances, such as injuries, were to befall their receivers. But now Beckham has openly criticized the team and that could be a problem. Most teams, you see, don't want to re-sign players that have been publicly critical of them. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson exits game vs. Titans with ankle injury
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson did not start the second half of Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans because of an ankle injury.
articles.body: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson did not start the second half of Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans because of an ankle injury. Jackson was on the sideline without a helmet during the Ravens’ first possession of the third quarter, with Baltimore holding a 24-7 lead at the time. The team announced that he was questionable to return. Jackson was off to a hot start before leaving. He completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the first half. He also carried the ball twice for 20 yards. He was tackled on the second-to-last play of the half and appeared to be favoring his ankle after going to the sideline. He was replaced by backup Tyler Huntley to start the third quarter. Injuries have been an issue at times for Jackson, a two-time MVP. He missed four games last year, and the Ravens went only 2-2 in his absence. Baltimore finished the 2025 season 8-9 and missed the playoffs. In 2021, Jackson missed five games, and the Ravens went 1-4 without him, missing the playoffs. The following season, he again missed five games and didn’t play in Baltimore’s first-round playoff loss. The Ravens entered this season with high expectations despite parting ways with previous head coach John Harbaugh. He was replaced by former Los Angeles Chargers defensive coordinator Jesse Minter, who was a defensive coach under Harbaugh in Baltimore from 2017 to 2020. The Ravens entered Sunday with a 2-1 record, defeating the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys with their only loss coming against the New Orleans Saints. Jackson, 29, is in his ninth season with Baltimore, which selected him with the final pick of the first round in the 2018 NFL draft. Entering Sunday, he had thrown for 745 yards and four touchdowns this season and run for one more score. Jackson is the second-to-last year of a five-year, $260 million contract he signed in March 2023. He and the Raven reportedly did not seriously discuss a long-term extension before this season.

articles.title: NFL writer Arif Hasan on his viral Jameis Winston column: ‘I have been thinking about this one for a while’
articles.summary: Some view New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston as fun-loving and goofy, while others see him quite differently. The Heisman Trophy winner and a former...
articles.body:
Some view New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston as fun-loving and goofy, while others see him quite differently.

The Heisman Trophy winner and a former No. 1 overall draft pick never lived up to expectations in the NFL. However, after Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury, he is now the New York Giants' starting quarterback. He's also building a media career, having served as a World Cup correspondent for Fox Sports .

That's not the whole Winston story, as he has faced accusations of mistreating women on several occasions. He was suspended for the first three games of 2018 after the NFL said its investigation found that Winston inappropriately touched a female Uber driver . In 2012, Winston was accused of sexual assault at Florida State. No charges were ever filed, but Winston and his accuser did settle a federal lawsuit .

When we look at Winston now, are we seeing the full picture?

Recently, Arif Hasan wrote a piece for The Guardian about Winston that struck a nerve and garnered 2.5 million views on X. We spoke with Hasan, who runs Wide Left , a newsletter covering the NFL , about his column.

Note: This interview has been edited and condensed for length and clarity.

Arif Hasan: "It's primarily been positive. A lot of people have appreciated that I've written a story. A lot of people have expressed interest in seeing someone cover something like this, or in wanting to write it themselves at the outlets they cover. I would say probably 95% of the reaction has been appreciative of having the story written."

" The Guardian reached out to me asking if I was interested in doing freelance work. I said that I was interested, and I wondered what kind of pitches they were looking for from someone like me. They mentioned a couple of story ideas and brought up the Jameis one. I was like, 'Well, actually, I have been thinking about this one for a while.'

"So, I worked it back and forth with them because I remember a lot of the stuff happening during the World Cup, a lot of the really goofy interactions, especially that he had with the Netherlands fans and stuff like that. A couple of my friends on various social media feeds were expressing a little bit of disgust about seeing him plastered all over, given his history. Putting that together, I saw interest in talking about Winston having an elevated public presence, especially now that he's starting for the New York Giants. It felt like good timing, a story that I've been kind of interested in covering and I've been thinking about for a little while, and that he's had a lot of publicity recently as a result."

What are your thoughts about how Jameis Winston is portrayed?

"I think that he's big, charismatic, and silly, and I think that's kind of a significant part of the way he's put forward. If you take a look at the editing in these World Cup videos, a lot of it focuses on some physical comedy, like he hits his head on the top of the bus and they make a fun noise about it. He mixes up his words a fair amount. He's smiling all the time, and they really like to emphasize all of that. So, I think just being silly, being a jester and getting people to talk to him, I think that he's characterized as somebody fun and easygoing and funny."

Why do you think he's received these opportunities, especially given his background?

"I think, genuinely, it's an archetype that's kind of difficult to find in football. I'm referring to the silly, goofy guy. Fox specifically has found some success with that: Rob Gronkowski and Terry Bradshaw. They like that archetype. It's actually pretty difficult to find someone who's funny in an approachable way. I mean, there's no denying that he's very charismatic. I think that's rare because football culture trains its athletes to be organized, more private, not to be very public with their statements, not to be very explosive, and to be very team-forward and team-oriented. We don't have a lot of opportunities to see people with a lot of personality, especially funny, silly personalities."

Does Winston deserve these opportunities?

"I think everyone's going to come to that decision on their own. But for me personally, I would say no.

"I am a big believer in second chances. That's why I bring up Michael Vick at the end of my story for The Guardian . But I do think there needs to be some accounting for behavior. There needs to be some level of contrition. And I understand that it puts him in a pretty dicey spot where it is difficult to put together a public statement without admitting liability, and circumstances where he continues to maintain his innocence. And so that's a difficult thing to resolve for him when it comes to someone like me.

"But I think this pattern of behavior is strong enough that it's really difficult to look at what he's alleged to have done and see somebody who is contrite about his behavior. And so, for me, the precondition to that is to show genuine concern for women's welfare or the culture of athletics that really diminishes the voices of survivors. Because we see this all the time; it's not just in athletics, but it's very prominent in athletics. We see this all the time where women allege some kind of traumatic behavior from an athlete, or are pushed aside or bullied out.

"I think that having a discussion about that from his end would, I think, go a long way toward helping me understand that this is somebody worth having a different image. And as I wrote in the piece, no one is required to accept Vick's contrition or apology, but at least he engaged in that."

Why should your average fan care about what you've written?

"If you care about a society that's healthy and respects everybody in it, you need to take a look at aspects of society that are uncomfortable, and approach it head-on. … We see this in politics. We see this in our personal lives. I think this is just one aspect of it. This is one facet of it. And I think if you're a fan of the NFL, you see it fairly often. It normalizes our treatment of women or anybody who's in a vulnerable position. If we continue to promote people without acknowledgment of some of the things some of these people have done, it feels like it just ultimately doesn't matter until it becomes unambiguous and on video, like with the Ray Rice situation. I think that we (should) care because (if not) it creates a culture of us not caring. I think that we all are invested in a society that pays attention to the most vulnerable among us."

You said most responses to your column have been positive. What about the negative feedback?

"There were a couple. When this was originally reported, there were a lot of enthusiastic—maybe the best way to put it—Florida State fans who were harassing people who were talking about it. I was a little worried I would see that, but I didn't. I didn't see that very much at all. But I still saw people who were like, 'Why now? Why are you comfortable ruining someone's career? Why aren't you covering X, Y, Z, other person who's alleged to have committed these offenses? Is this racialized in some way? Why aren't you talking about white people who do this?' I think that, to the extent that coverage of these sorts of incidents can be particularized or racialized in ways that are pretty problematic and significant, there is something to be said about that. But I also don't think that is a good reason not to discuss this particular facet of this particular person."

How do you think perceptions of Winston will continue to evolve now that he's the Giants' starting quarterback?

"The more success he has, the bigger his profile will be. I think you're right that, given the stature of the New York Giants within the media and within coverage, it's really significant every time anybody suits up for them, especially as the starting quarterback. I think success there is going to be really big in terms of improving his image. I was going to use the word rehabilitating. I don't think that's correct. I think one of the issues, the reason I wrote the piece, is because his image is already so positive. It doesn't need rehabilitation. But in terms of preparing him for kind of a national media stage, I think that more success there is going to do a lot to create an environment that is going to be very easy for Fox Sports to put him central to whatever coverage that they want to put him into."

What key takeaway do you hope readers get from your column?

"I think the takeaway is that it doesn't necessarily have to be about Jameis Winston specifically, but about how readily we accept harmful or problematic behavior from people we put on a pedestal. We should always be open to critiques of those people, no matter how beneficial they've been to our lives or how much we like them."

articles.title: Cam Bynum: Commanders fans traveled better than any overseas crowd he’s seen
articles.summary: Commanders fans turned Tottenham Hotspur Stadium into a home-field atmosphere, but the Colts still left London with a 30-13 victory.
articles.body:
LONDON – The Washington Commanders were declared the home team for Sunday's Week 4 contest against the Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium the moment the NFL released its schedule in May. Commanders fans from both sides of the Atlantic made that abundantly clear.

In what represented a change of pace from the team's first three international regular-season games – the Colts played the Jaguars in England in 2016 and the Patriots (2023) and Falcons (2025) in Germany – Indianapolis was without question the road team from an atmosphere standpoint, backing up observations reporters had made in recent days roaming the city in the number and passion of Commanders supporters.

Whether it was due to an extra large group of locals who've grown to support the Commanders, or a sizable contingent making the hop across the pond, is unclear, but Colts players noticed the discrepancy from the moment they jogged out of the tunnel Sunday.

Indianapolis Colts vs Washington Commanders photos in NFL Week 4 action

Running out onto the field first pregame, as is tradition for a road team, the Colts were overwhelmingly booed by the crowd.

The Commanders? The roar of the crowd mixed with a formal hype video on the big-screens around the stadium as maroon and gold flares shot off into the sky. What had typically been a neutral crowd during the NFL's nearly two decades of playing regular season games on an international stage transformed Sunday into a home-field advantage for the Commanders.

"I think out of all the teams I've played overseas, (the Commanders) is the fanbase that traveled the best that I've seen," Colts safety Camryn Bynum said. "Maybe that's because they're on the east coast, and so it's a closer flight?

"But it is still six hours (away) for them, so I don't know. They did travel really well."

Bynum came to Berlin in his first season with the Colts last November for a game where the Colts were listed as the home team – the only instance the franchise has been the designated home team. In his previous stint with the Vikings, Bynum has been on the 'away' team (2022 against the Saints) and the 'home' team (2024 against the Jets) – both at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Both teams had home-base bars in the heart of London this week. For what it's worth, the Commanders opted to make the trip on Tuesday and spent their entire game week – including all three practices – in the city. The Colts arrived Friday morning and went through an afternoon walk-through. Head coach Shane Steichen termed the game all week as a "business trip," and with just more than 48 hours in the town, players largely kept to the team's headquarters at Hanbury Manor Marriott Hotel & Country Club an hour north of downtown London.

Throughout Sunday's game, the Colts were the opposition of fan chants while pro-Commanders videos and messages ran on repeat on the big screens. Though a representation of most – and maybe all – 32 NFL teams' jerseys could be seen with a quick scan of the fans in attendance, the scenery at-large was deeply maroon-colored among the more than 60,000 fans in attendance.

"I think for me, every time we play overseas, it's enjoyable because the fans are so passionate about everything. You see people wearing a bunch of different jerseys because they're just football fans, and the fans here really understand the game so well and it gets really loud when people make plays," Bynum said. "I love playing out here.

"This is a long road win, but I love it. Anytime I can play overseas, I see it as a free vacation. We just have to play our favorite sport in the world, so for me, it's all fun. Obviously, we come out here to win, but if I could play out here every week or play somewhere overseas every week, I personally would."

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase ruled out with concussion in Week 4
articles.summary: Ja'Marr Chase took a big hit after a face-mask penalty.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase was forced into the blue medical tent early against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 4. He later left the contest to be evaluated for a concussion.

After being initially declared as questionable to return, Chase was ruled out of the game at the start of the third quarter.

Chase was injured on a second-quarter drive. With the Bengals pushing down the field, Chase caught a quick pass and looked to turn the ball up the field. As he tried to break away from a defender, Chase had his face mask grabbed.

As he was going to the ground, Chase was hit hard by another defender.

The All-Pro wideout went into the blue medical tent on the sideline and missed the rest of the drive. The Bengals settled for a field goal, tying things 3-3.

Chase was then spotted walking off the field and heading to the team's locker room, where he was initially deemed questionable to return. Coming out of halftime, however, Chase was ruled out for the rest of the game. He finished the contest with three catches for 27 yards.

Chase must not have been feeling too bad, as he sent out a tweet during the fourth quarter of the contest.

It's unclear whether Chase will face punishment for the tweet, as player are typically prohibited from posting on social media during games.
